match_pca — 3D match_pose op

• Data kinds: points × points → pose

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.match_pca(pts_scene, pts_model) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.match_pca(pts_scene, pts_model); from the registry, ops3d.get("match_pca"))

Usage

PCA pose matching (structure = point cloud × method = principal-axis alignment).

Returns a coarse rigid transform (rotation R + translation t) that aligns the principal axes of both clouds. It handles the rotation that NCC/phase correlation cannot (the 4-way sign ambiguity is resolved by least squares. That residual is a coarse criterion assuming the points of both clouds correspond in the same order — for measured clouds without correspondence, refine downstream with ICP or similar). Returns (R(3,3), t(3,)).

Meaning of the return value: pts_scene ≈ (R @ pts_model.T).T + t (t = c_scene − R·c_model). R is always a rotation with det=+1 (no reflections). The residual is measured by pairing points in index order, so for clouds without correspondence the choice among the 4 candidates is unreliable (in that case pass it as init_R/init_t to icp_point2point_3d to refine). For clouds whose principal axes are degenerate (equal eigenvalues, such as a sphere or cylinder) the axes are undefined and the result is unstable. The two clouds may have different point counts. Input is (N,3) (validation is left to moment_axes; there is none).
